claims.claim: Rust model Bash lacks background and stdin parameters.
claims.finding: Model-facing Rust Bash is foreground-only. Rust interactive user Bash has an asynchronous task and cancellation slot, so background-like user execution must not be called wholly missing.

claims.claim: Automatic/manual release, a <=16 running registry, completion and cleanup.
claims.finding: Immediate explicit launches enforce 16 running shells; foreground adoption/release is not covered by that admission guard. Finished non-lingering retention is 20 in adoption order; lingering jobs remain. User-kill synthetic completion omits ordinary log/exit/lingering fields, and late settlement is ignored. Full-log creation/removal and process cleanup require distinct contracts.

claims.claim: bash_output/kill/input controls, waiting limits and input denied without UI.
claims.finding: Tool names and high-level limits are correct. No-UI denial applies to approval='ask'; allow bypasses confirmation. Exact wait/cursor/tail/grep, running-state checks, byte budgets and return schemas are specified in the entries.

claims.claim: Pattern/silence/interval watches, <=16 watches, <=10 fires and defaults.
claims.finding: Explicit create limits do not bound automatically installed default watches. Pattern defaults to one fire; other explicit watches default to three, with maximum ten. Explicit silence minimum is 5 seconds, while automatic silence settings follow their separate policy. Timed prompt detection, fire IDs, rearm/carry and cleanup are material omitted contracts; session owns alert delivery/wake.

claims.claim: Shells panel and RPC background controls/events.
claims.finding: Tool registry interfaces are covered by TOOLS; RPC-026 covers named shell controls/events, and published TUI-055 supplies the shell-panel contract. Native asynchronous user-Bash streaming/cancellation is preserved; it does not imply a native model-facing background registry.

Rust already has a bounded 64-message RPC writer with ordered drain and failure cancellation. It lacks stdout isolation, individual/aggregate UTF-8 byte reservations, typed limit errors, transient 10 ms retries and guard lifecycle; print mode drops sink failures. Context breakdown and usage totals remain other-area claims.

rust_only.ts_comparison: TS default find and grep provision fd/rg; Rust traverses and matches in process. Preserve that backend choice while implementing TOOLS-028/029/030 observable semantics.

rust_only.capability: MutatingEnv capability boundary and queue held through mutation I/O
rust_only.ts_comparison: Keep Rust's explicit mutation capability and lock lifetime while adding invocation-order/canonical-alias parity.

rust_only.capability: Native image processing without Photon worker/WASM
rust_only.ts_comparison: The Rust image backend can remain native; its corrected orientation-aware no-transform condition is valuable. TOOLS-023 separates backend choice from MIME/quality/resize/coordinate differences.

rust_only.capability: Additional edit input compatibility and duplicate-match context
rust_only.ts_comparison: Rust accepts single edit objects and JSON-string objects and returns richer ambiguity context; current TS normalizes legacy flat input and JSON array strings. Preserve intentional Rust compatibility while fixing exact precedence.

Outside the seven-name TS factories inspected here, Rust exports a Windows-only PowerShell tool using UTF-16LE base64 EncodedCommand, fixed noninteractive options and capture cancellation/timeout. Preserve it; this is a factory comparison, not a claim that no TS extension can supply PowerShell.
Retain the 64-message channel, blocking sink isolation, ordered drain and failure cancellation while adding the distinct TOOLS-031 byte-budget/isolation contract.
